scenes.narration: If an executive earns one million dollars in salary, federal and state income taxes immediately claim nearly half before a single dollar is invested. Yet when a founder holding one hundred million dollars in appreciating equity needs cash to fund a new venture or buy real estate, they rarely sell a single share.

Selling appreciated stock triggers an immediate taxable event. Under current capital gains rules, liquidating a multi-million dollar position converts paper wealth into realized income, permanently shrinking the compounding base that generates future returns. To avoid breaking that compounding engine, institutional wealth relies on a structural alternative.

Financial planners refer to this three-stage lifecycle as Buy, Borrow, Die. First, capital is allocated into durable, cash-flowing or appreciating assets such as index equities, commercial real estate, or private equity. Rather than harvesting gains through sales, the portfolio is pledged as collateral to a private bank.

Because borrowed money is a liability rather than earned income, loan proceeds are not taxed when disbursed. If a portfolio grows at eight percent annually while a securities-backed credit line charges five percent interest, the borrower retains liquidity while their underlying equity continues compounding uninterrupted.

However, this mechanism carries severe downside risk when markets contract. Every securities-backed loan enforces a strict loan-to-value threshold. If equity prices drop thirty percent during a recession, the lender issues an immediate margin call, forcing the borrower to post additional cash or watch their assets liquidated at the bottom.

The final stage occurs upon estate transfer. Under stepped-up cost basis provisions in jurisdictions like the United States, inherited assets reset their tax baseline to fair market value at the date of transfer, erasing decades of unrealized capital gains. Understanding these structural incentives explains why asset ownership outpaces wage income over multi-decade horizons.
